teaser: Programming by voice, chat, phone, IDE and pull request, with one shared state underneath, at every stage from explorer to town planner. This site, counted.
core_idea: Programming has become multichannel: voice memos, chat, phones, IDEs, pull requests, previews and vaults; it becomes omnichannel, in the retail sense Rigby described in 2011, when every channel reads and writes one shared state, git, vaults, briefs and graphs; this site is the worked example, 54 messages in and 40 releases out in three days; review and custom interfaces are channels too; it works for explorers, villagers and town planners at every altitude; it is already how a new generation builds; and it breaks through fragmentation, misplaced secrets and lost context, which the shared state fixes.

figures.caption: Multichannel and omnichannel programming: on the left, each channel keeps its own copy of the work and a person carries the context between them; on the right, every channel reads and writes one shared state, so work started in one continues in any other.

One session, many channels: what this newsroom session used from 13 to 15 October 2026, counted from its transcript and the repository log: what came in, what went out, what it was checked against, what kept it safe, and how I read it back, all around one shared state.

Omnichannel at every stage of a Wardley map: explorers, villagers and town planners each use all the channels, at every altitude from voice and intent, through interfaces and code, down to evidence. What changes between stages is what the work needs, not the channel.
